newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-OPINION - Inside Canberra - Howard's Canberra-to-Sydney shuttle.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-OPINION - Inside Canberra - Howard's Canberra-to-Sydney shuttle.

text.p: (From the "Inside Canberra" newsletter)
The uneasy feeling in Melbourne that Sydney has become the de facto capital will be strengthened by latest figures on prime ministerial travel.
In the 113 days between March 8 and June 28 John Howard made 31 round trips between Sydney and Canberra using the Dassault Falcon 900 of the RAAF VIP squadron.
Thus for 16 weeks on average he spent three and a half days in the national capital.
The government has decided not to proceed with scheduled refurbishment work at The Lodge in Canberra in view of Howard taking up permanent residence at Kirribilli House.
One of Howard's favorite taunts of Keating was that he was a part time Prime Minister.
It can certainly be said that Canberra has become the part time national capital.
Howard's shuttling back and forth between Sydney and Canberra in those 113 days cost the taxpayer A$55,000.
Mind you he was accompanied by staff as well.
In fact, assuming he was always accompanied by three staff, his 31 trips by Ansett or Qantas would have totalled A$57,288 on the basis of a first class return air fare of A$462.

Howard, when replying to criticism about the cost of his living in Kirribilli House stated: "I have absolutely no intention of committing the Australian taxpayer to any unreasonable additional expense and I think that you will find that, on the other side of the ledger, there are quite significant savings in the new living arrangements."
We await with interest the details of these savings.
EUTHANASIA AND NORTHERN TERRITORY STATEHOOD

One thing is certain, should backbencher Kevin Andrews' private member's bill to overturn the Northern Territory euthanasia legislation be carried in federal parliament, the NT will not get self-government while John Howard is prime minister.
The achievement of self-government is the top priority of the Shane Stone Country-Liberal Party NT Government.
Howard obviously feels deeply about overturning the NT euthanasia law -- why else would he have personally sponsored Andrews private members bill in the House of Representatives?
Without Howard's support the bill would not have even been debated.
Should the NT achieve statehood it would then have the constitutional power to pass euthanasia legislation free of interference from the Federal Parliament.
The MP making all the running against Andrews (and therefore Howard) is Chris Gallus, the Liberal backbencher for the seat of Hindmarsh (SA).
Gallus was Shadow Minister for Aboriginal Affairs in Opposition and accompanied Alexander Downer, when he was Liberal Leader, on his disastrous trip to inland Australia to meet Aborigines.
Gallus was dumped from the front bench by Howard when he formed his ministry.
(Views here are those of Inside Canberra, not Reuters)
-- Inside Canberra 61-6 273-1600
